_comment: Pre-baked presenter loops. Drop an MP4 in this folder and move an entry into
'avatars' below; no code change is needed. An entry whose file is missing is
skipped with a warning, so it is safe to list avatars before generating them.
'avatars' is empty by default, which disables the presenter and renders the
normal full-width layout. To try it, copy the entry from '_example_entry'
into 'avatars' — placeholder_m01.mp4 ships in this folder for exactly that.
Required fields: avatar_id, file, languages, source, licence, disclosure_label.
'source' must be one of: synthetic | licensed_stock | consented_performer.
Animating a real, identifiable official's likeness is not permitted — that is
a deepfake of a named public figure, and no disclosure label makes it
acceptable for government communications. avatar_registry rejects any other
'disclosure_label' is rendered on screen for the whole time the presenter is
visible. README section 21 requires computer-narrated output to be labelled;
a photoreal presenter makes that requirement stronger, not weaker.
'languages' accepts language codes and '*' as a catch-all.
Clips should be 6-12s, seamlessly looping, H.264 yuv420p. Portrait framing
suits the panel best; landscape clips are centre-cropped to fit.

_example_entry.licence: Procedurally generated placeholder, no real person depicted

_language_assignment_note: Which presenter fronts which language is a product decision, not a technical
one - the split below is arbitrary, chosen only so all three get exercised.
resolve() takes an exact language match first and falls back to '*', so
moving a code between entries is the whole change.
presenter_03 has no .gestures.json sidecar on purpose: it is a tight
head-and-shoulders shot whose hands are out of frame almost throughout, so
there is no gesture vocabulary to map. It loops straight through instead,
which is the documented behaviour for an unsegmented avatar.
